_README.what: Props are in-world documents you can open. An item record says a ledger exists; a prop lets the reader read it. Rendered by renderProp() in index.html, styled by app/styles/systems/exhibits.css.
where_they_appear: Inline in any prose field, via the marker [[prop:<id>|visible text]] — becomes a clickable .proplink.
As a tile grid on the item page of every item listed in the prop's `items` array.
As an 'Exhibits' card at the foot of any article listed in the prop's `articles` array.
_README.adding_one: Add an object here, give it `kind`, `title`, `body` (HTML using the .pd-* classes) and at least one link in `items` or `articles`. No JS or CSS changes are needed. Keep the body factual to the source record — a prop is evidence, not new canon.
_README.stamps: Optional. `stamps: ["overdue"]` renders .pd-stamp--overdue. Available: overdue, paid, void, sealed, noaction, evidence.

Field Report — militia hand, unsigned
Written during the snowfall · stamped by Central Command three days later
URGENT
Commander, the snow is humming. I repeat, the snow is humming.
The village elder tried speaking to it, but the well froze solid in seconds.
Requesting immediate tactical support.
RECEIVED — Central Command — three days after the date written above.
The ink is smeared and the parchment is still cold to the touch. A report that takes three days to be received was either not sent when it was written, or not opened when it arrived. Both readings are worse than a slow courier. — W.
Filed. The elder is not named anywhere in this file. — WAH.

prop_ebot_correction_demand.title: Correction Demand — Sheet 41
prop_ebot_correction_demand.subtitle: Filed 1032 BF · acknowledged by a clerk · never answered
prop_ebot_correction_demand.note: The demand was posted, acknowledged, and never acted upon. The Company later burned down with its plates inside, which is why Survey Series IV can no longer be corrected by anybody at any price.
prop_ebot_correction_demand.body:
Walupedia Editorial Board
Office of the Auditor-General
To
The Works Manager, The Old World Mapping Company
Re
Survey Series IV, Sheet 41 — defective plate
Dated
19 Aethel, 1032 BF

Sir,

Your Sheet 41 names the mountain at the head of the Northern Reach MOUNT EBOT. The mountain is correctly Mount Ebot. The mountain your customers believe they are buying is Mount Ebott, which lies four hundred miles east of it, and which contains a barrier, a quantity of monsters, and a king with a beard.

Your cartouche offers corrections on application. This is the application.

On the seventeenth of this month a party of three reached the summit of your Sheet 41 on the strength of your spelling. A chartered aircraft was destroyed. A twenty-two-year-old man was opened above the eye by a thrown bone and dressed under an overhang in hail. He was promised nothing and has so far received it.

Waluigi does not ask for damages. Waluigi asks for a T.

Correct the plate. Reissue the sheet. Every copy still folded in a saddlebag is a hazard you engraved.

Waluigi
Auditor-General
 
For the Company — no reply received
Acknowledged by a clerk, 24 Aethel 1032. Nothing further. Works destroyed by fire; plates lost. — filed to archive 1040 BF

prop_xo_stage_card.body:
ACT TWO

ENTRANCE. Not through the door. Through the door is what they are watching.

LIGHT. Behind. Always behind. A face explained is a face diminished.

THE LINE. Delivered once. If it must be repeated the scene has already failed and the failure is theirs.

Read it twice. The fourth line selects a victim by how well they will describe the event afterwards. That is not vanity. That is target selection. — W.

prop_toad_lee_diary_page.title: Diary Page — Lady Aurelian, on Grafting

prop_toad_lee_diary_page.body:
Diary of Lady Aurelian · loose page, preserved

They call it grafting, which is a gardener's word, and they chose it on purpose. A graft takes. A graft is not a wound, it is a joining, and the tree does not complain afterwards because the tree has nothing left to complain with.

What is joined is not the flesh. Anyone can join flesh. What is joined is the line — and a line that has been joined once can be joined again, which is the part they do not say aloud at the table.

The Legion watches the wrong end of it. They watch the bodies. The bodies are the least interesting part. Watch the blood-work, and watch who is keeping the record of it, because whoever keeps that record decides afterwards what happened.

A.
Unsigned beyond the initial
Reading is a combat skill. This page connects Legion observation to Corvinarus blood-work and it was recovered by the party member most famous for a window. — W.

prop_tea_syndicate_page.title: The Third Steeping — House Doctrine
prop_tea_syndicate_page.subtitle: A page from the Tea Leaf Syndicate book · read by Eager, absorbed by nobody
prop_tea_syndicate_page.note: Tea people made hot leaf water into doctrine. Waluigi is annoyed and impressed, in that order, and only just.
prop_tea_syndicate_page.body:
The Tea Leaf Syndicate
On the Third Steeping · House Doctrine, Article the Ninth
i. The first steeping is for the guest. It is courteous, it is weak, and it tells you nothing.
ii. The second steeping is for the table. By it a house is judged, and by it a house intends to be judged, which is why the second steeping is never the truth.
iii. The third steeping is for the business. It is taken after the guest has said the thing they came to say and before they have decided whether they meant it.
iv. A leaf held too long turns bitter and cannot be made sweet again by any subsequent kindness. The Syndicate applies this to leaves and to people and considers the comparison exact.
v. Serve the third steeping yourself. A cup poured by a servant is a cup poured by whoever pays the servant.
Preparations not found in polite markets are treated in Articles the Eleventh through Fourteenth, which are not reproduced here and which the archive has not seen.
Clause v is genuine operational security dressed as etiquette. Eager read this page and learned nothing, which is also data. — W.

prop_necromancer_wand_demand.body:
The Mages Guild
Office of Restricted Foci · correspondence

To the King of the Koopas, wherever this finds him,

It has come to the Guild’s attention that an object dropped by the claimant Vivian during the corridor engagement at the Shadow Estate — a focus of death aspect, cold to the touch, of a make the Guild recognises and does not admire — was subsequently retrieved from the floor by yourself.

The Guild does not suggest that you took it improperly. The Guild observes only that it was on the floor and you are, by all accounts, a person who picks things up.

Such foci are corruptive by design. They reward curiosity and they punish it in the same motion. The Guild would ordinarily write at length here about the risk to the bearer’s mind, and has prepared four paragraphs to that effect, which have been struck at the request of a colleague who has met you.

We ask that the focus be surrendered to any Guild station. We do not ask that it be studied, demonstrated, pointed at anyone, used to settle an argument, or kept because it is interesting.

Awaiting your reply, without confidence,

Keeper of Restricted Foci
The Mages Guild
No reply was sent. Waluigi suspects the wand is more disturbed by Bowser than Bowser is by the wand, and that this is the safest containment the Guild will ever achieve by accident. — W.

Waluigi records the following for completeness, though it is probably not significant.

The neighbor left in a hurry, right? Like someone called him. And when I was leaving the basement, I saw his desk upstairs — the one near the front door. There was a communicator on it. Still active. Still connected. And there was a voice coming through it. Faint. But I heard it.

Waluigi asked what the voice said.

It said, "Professor, it's happening again. He's emerged. We need the contingency." And then it said a name.

Waluigi asked what name.

It said "Mr. L."

Wario paused.

And then it said: "Activate Protocol Green Thunder."

Waluigi asked Wario why he had not mentioned this in the previous two tellings. Wario shrugged and said: "You didn't ask."

Waluigi has no additional commentary on this addendum. Waluigi is not going to think about it. Waluigi is moving on.

prop_archie_dream_addendum.body:
Walupedia Editorial Board
Classification ruling · main chronicle vs. footnote
Attached after filing — the placement was challenged and the challenge failed

A lesser historian would place this in a footnote and call it psychological color. Waluigi is not a lesser historian.

Objects appearing in the dream that are live files elsewhere in this archive:

ObjectAlso filed under
Star ShardsArtifacts — active recovery
Star CoreArtifacts — hesitation on record
Frog GodDivine consequence — the abandoned Toad
EagerHostage leverage — ongoing
HjumpikTrust imagery
Original DanPersonal consequence — entanglement
The VigilanceAirship — burning, in the dream
The Dreadful GroveLocation — storm magic

If a dream contains that many active files, it is no longer color. It is a filing cabinet on fire.

The dream also connects two kinds of consequence. The Frog God is the cosmic result of Archie abandoning the Toad. Original Dan is the personal result of Archie being tangled in another person's destruction. The dream forces Archie to face both, then wakes him where the current party crisis continues. That is structure. Cruel structure, but structure.

Standing recommendation
1. Archie should tell someone immediately — not later, not after three jokes and one accidental tactical disaster.
2. Told, the dream becomes shared preparation.
3. Kept private, it remains the Frog God's rehearsal room inside his skull — and privacy lets shame edit the useful parts.
Waluigi prefers enemy rehearsals to be interrupted.
WAH.

Walupedia Editorial Board
Addendum · Feyward branch assessment
Attached to the session record — the session did not close the branch

Waluigi wants to be clear that this session did not resolve the Feyward branch. It made the Feyward branch more legible. That is different and, in some ways, more useful.

A solved problem stops moving. A legible problem can be hunted.

SubjectBefore the sessionAfter
Toad LeeUseful, occasionally ridiculousUseful, ridiculous, and a possible security problem
Mystic MorelAmbiguous presenceAntagonist and informant — appeared from a wall, survived near-decapitation, issued a targeted warning, provided a key

The revelOngoingStill ongoing

Money is not the only thing characters carry. They carry obligations. They carry evidence. They carry debts that never entered a ledger because the person who issued them smiled instead of writing them down.

Waluigi will track both, because Waluigi knows that unrecorded debts are how people end up dancing forever.

Somebody wanted this man for one thing, failed to get him for it, and re-engraved the reason rather than withdraw the reward. The reward is the constant. The offence is the variable. Waluigi would like that sentence read twice. — W.

prop_archmage_requisition.subtitle: The Guild billed for the elixir and separately for the indignity
prop_archmage_requisition.note: The Guild will do almost anything if you make staying polite more expensive than complying.

The Guild invented a line item for being stood over, priced it at three hundred gold, and then wrote the whole bill off rather than go and find the dwarf. Waluigi has never respected an institution less or a dwarf more. — W.

prop_dragon_barter_note.subtitle: Written on the reverse of a ration chit by a party who could not read the front
prop_dragon_barter_note.note: The dragon believed it had the better of this. Waluigi is not certain the dragon was wrong.

Reverse of a ration chit

Note on the spotted variety. The spotted kind is a controlled reagent below the capital. Six bags of it moved across a table, unremarked, as the worthless half of a trade.
Two parties each walked away certain they had cheated the other, and the archive’s view is that they were both right, which is the only kind of trade Waluigi genuinely enjoys reading about. — W.

prop_ashford_transcript.title: Testimony — The Ashford Spirit, As Relayed
prop_ashford_transcript.subtitle: Transcribed at one remove. The archive says so at the top rather than the bottom.
prop_ashford_transcript.note: The only testimony this file has, and it arrives through a hand the archive cannot identify.
prop_ashford_transcript.body:
Relayed testimony · second-hand by admission
Notes in a hand resembling Luigi’s. Not authenticated.
“The coronations were theatre. Real power signed in blood not ink. What was signed is sealed in iron, beneath the hanging tree, in the Thornwood.”
Speaker
Ashford, deceased, manifesting
Relay
Notes taken by a third party at the time; hand not authenticated
Corroboration
None. No second hearer has been produced.
On the phrase signed in blood not ink. Capable of two readings. Figurative: a settlement enforced by violence. Literal: an instrument executed in blood, which is a documentary form with a shelf life and a smell, and which iron would be a sensible container for.
On the phrase theatre. Capable of only one reading, and it is the useful one. Theatre has a budget.
Filed under protest. Waluigi objects to the whole class of evidence and has filed it anyway, because refusing to file the only testimony you have is not scepticism, it is squeamishness.

prop_satyr_songsheet.title: Song Sheet — Two Verses, One Written Over the Other
prop_satyr_songsheet.subtitle: A performer's working copy, with the correction still legible underneath
prop_satyr_songsheet.note: The verse the satyr sang and the verse the satyr crossed out are both on this sheet, and only one of them was safe.
prop_satyr_songsheet.body:
Performer’s working sheet
Recovered from the pit. Two hands, or one hand twice.
“Oh the Legion marches iron-shod,
and the Legion answers to the rod,
and the rod is held by a living god
and the rod is held by the ones abroad.”
Struck line. Legible beneath the correction. Written in the same ink and the same hand as the rest of the verse.
Replacement line. Written in a harder pressure and slightly cramped, as though fitted into a space that was already the wrong size.
Performed. The replacement. Witnesses agree the Legion danced.
A satyr sang a room full of soldiers into a dance, and the only edit on the sheet is the line that would have told them who holds the rod. He changed it before he walked in, not during. That is not stage fright, that is a risk assessment. — W.

prop_goblin_parole.title: Parole Note — One Guard, Spared, Released on Terms
prop_goblin_parole.subtitle: Written by the man who was spared, at the request of the people who spared him
prop_goblin_parole.note: The party let a guard live and got a document out of it, which is a better return than most mercy earns.

Undertaking, given freely
Hand: the maker’s own, unsteady, in charcoal

“I was on the door. They did not kill me. I said I would write what I know and I am writing it.

The orders for the hall came down two days before, not that night. We were told there would be a performance and we were told not to interfere with it. I do not know who told the captain. The captain was pleased about it.

Two days before. That is the whole exhibit. The Legion did not spontaneously dance to a satyr — the Legion had been told, in advance, to permit a performance it had no reason to expect. — W.

prop_speaker_l_decoy_brief.title: Decoy Brief — What the Green Speaker Was to Say, and When to Stop
prop_speaker_l_decoy_brief.subtitle: A written plan for being the wrong person in the right room
prop_speaker_l_decoy_brief.note: The brief survives. Whether it was followed is a separate exhibit.
prop_speaker_l_decoy_brief.body:
Brief · for the speaker attending
Read, memorised, and not to be carried into the chamber
1. You are the delegation. There is no other delegation. If asked whether others are coming, say they are not.
2. Speak to the resettlement question at length. Detail is the point. The longer the chamber discusses where, the longer it is not discussing who.
3. If the words order and one hundred and twenty are used together, stop speaking, sit down, and do not answer further questions.
4. Do not defend anyone by name. A name in the record is a name on a list.
5. You will be believed because you are expected. That is the entire mechanism. Do not improve on it.
Clause 3 means somebody already knew the number before the chamber sat. A decoy brief that names the trigger phrase in advance is not a decoy brief, it is a warning that was written down. — W.

prop_avatar_terms_memo.title: Terms Memorandum — What Was Asked For, in Four Lines
prop_avatar_terms_memo.subtitle: Somebody in that circle wrote the terms down while they were still being spoken
prop_avatar_terms_memo.note: Every negotiation has one participant taking notes. This is theirs.

Memorandum · taken at the circle
Contemporaneous. Not agreed by any party.
Asked of us. That armed men of the Loyalist establishment be quartered within the district, permanently, and at the district’s request.
Offered to us. Recognition. Standing. The rite completed rather than abandoned.
Objected by one voice. “A garrison you asked for is still a garrison.”
Answered. “A garrison you asked for is a garrison you can un-ask.”
Not addressed. Whether the un-asking has any legal effect. Nobody in the circle raised the Mandate.
The objection and the answer are both good and only one of them is true. Waluigi has read clause 9 of the Mandate and can report that the un-asking is worth precisely nothing, and that nobody at the circle knew it. — W.

By authority · posted notice
Supernatural Sovereignty Act · summary for posting
The full text is available for inspection at the ward office

2. An undertaking given in the course of a rite is an undertaking for the purposes of clause 1.
3. The offence is complete on the giving. Performance is not required.
4. The offence is triable as sedition.
5. Where the undertaking is given collectively, every person present who did not dissent aloud is taken to have given it.
Posted this quarter. Ward office copy stamped and dated.
Clause 5 is the one that should frighten people and clause 3 is the one that should frighten lawyers. Everybody who stood in that circle and did not shout is, on the face of this notice, a seditionist. — W.

prop_tl_interrogation.title: Interrogation Record — The Green Prisoner
prop_tl_interrogation.subtitle: Four words, one poisoned mushroom, and nothing else for the file

Subject: prisoner presenting as Speaker L
Interviewing officer notes taken contemporaneously.
On appearance. Subject's colouring is markedly green. Asked to account for it. States he ate a poisoned mushroom and the colour changed.

This is not retribution's art, but the mending of the fractured heart.

A man in a cell explained restorative justice to the people torturing him and they wrote 'cult-like rhetoric' in the assessment box. He was not the Speaker and he was not raving. He was running out the clock, in verse, and it worked. — W.

Order 120
Issued under the authority of the officer commanding.

Officer commanding

Unsigned · smoke-scented · edges charred inward from three sides
SECRET HISTORY MARIO
Filed by Waluigi the same morning it appeared. No seal. No courier. No helpful explanation. The center survived better than the margins because somebody planned it that way.
Opening posture. The writer stages Mario as openly hostile, suspicious of Bowser, suspicious of Luigi, and perfectly willing to threaten a stranger for speaking too slowly.
Claim one. When the questioner says Peach is dead and asks whether grief drove him east, Mario replies: “I didn't leave because of grief. I left because I killed her.”
Claim two. The note produces a gold locket with Peach and Mario pictured together and insists a wedding certificate existed with Bowser as witness. The scene is written for maximum outrage and should be read with that in mind.
Claim three. Mario confirms the farm story only to break it: he says he stayed not for months or years but for three days, died there, and later answers the question of what happened next with “I woke up.”
Claim four. Asked about the Mages' Guild, Mario says yes. An arrest is attempted under Section 1.6 with a null cage. The note then describes three consecutive cage failures and Mario laughing at the third.
Claim five. When pressed about the Star Fountain meeting with Luigi, Mario answers at the end with a silent nod rather than a denial.
A forged confession is still evidence of what somebody wants the archive to stare at. Peach. The farm. The Guild. The fountain. All on one page, as if Waluigi did not already have enough enemies. — W.
The intervening stage directions are extravagant, ash-heavy, and emotionally manipulative. Waluigi files the claims, not the performance. The performance is obvious.

prop_green_t_threshold_parley.body:
Archive of the Waluipedia — Threshold Note
Subject: Green T · Place: the doorway of Tymnas’s cottage · 30 Harvestide 1040 BF
Witnesses: Markop, Feyward Dan, Salam, Remi · Compiled by the archivist · Not a deposition
OBSERVED, IN ORDER
1. The subject arrived from the storm line in the rain and was asked, in the doorway, whether he was real.
2. The questioning party yawned. All four witnesses volunteered this detail unprompted and none could explain why it was the part they kept.
3. The subject answered the question by discharging a pistol through the cottage window. The pane had been repaired within the hour. The repair did not survive the answer.
“Would a fake do that?”
4. A second test was offered and a third was cast: a reading for non-humanoid blood in the area. The subject did not glow throughout. The reading lit the forehead only, and nowhere else.
5. Asked what the residue on his face was, the subject answered: “Fairy? This is Mazebound. I got what I needed.” The answer was accepted by the subject and by no one else present.
6. Asked whether he would be let in, the subject was refused on the grounds that it sounded like a terrible idea. He was admitted afterwards, by a different party, once the refusal had stopped being the most dangerous option in the doorway.
A mark is not a replacement. Marks are acquired. The archive has no record of what touched that forehead, and the man it belongs to has no record of it either, and those two absences are not the same thing. — W.
Four witnesses, one agreed detail, and a spell that stopped early. Keep the door on the chain. — WAH.

1. Agent will proceed to the property and recover the sample material.

Three lines and no signature. Nobody forged the Directorate — the line answered, the operator knew his tracker, and the liquid was correctly classified the moment it was described. They forged one thing: whoever sent him. — W.

prop_bowser_painting_note.title: Handwritten Note — Power Stars, Paintings, and Ice Cream
prop_bowser_painting_note.subtitle: Delivered by a Koopa guard at the outer gate · carried folded for a day and a night
prop_bowser_painting_note.note: Addressed to Mario. Handed to Luigi. Read at a checkpoint, folded twice, and not mentioned to anybody until a stranger spotted the corner of it in a second-floor study eleven hours later.

Oh, hi there Mario! I hope you don't mind, but I had to take all of those power stars and seal them all away in those paintings. prop_promo_mario_newspaper_clipping.title: Newspaper Clipping — Promo Mario
prop_promo_mario_newspaper_clipping.subtitle: Abridged reading copy · publisher, byline and issue date unidentified
prop_promo_mario_newspaper_clipping.note: An abridged account of what the newspaper claims, not certified testimony. No original issue, photograph or souvenir has been authenticated by the archive.
prop_promo_mario_newspaper_clipping.body:
PROMO MARIO
Darian Marsh and Alistair of the Marshkeepers — reported visitors
Claimed setting: Hollywood / Los Angeles, “1996”. This is the report's foreign dating, not an established equivalent of any BF date.
Lord Darian Marsh of the Dark Shores and his steward Alistair fell into filming of the Nintendo Mania pilot. Mario welcomed them, demonstrated Super Mario 64 and led them onto Hollywood Boulevard. Alistair gathered a souvenir shirt, ticket stub, soda can and churro stick; Mario took a group photograph with a disposable camera.
Darian produced a Wario Inc. tablet displaying Waluigi's account of the missing Mushroom Kingdom hero. Reading it, Mario dropped his phone and cried. Asked his full name, he offered “Mario... Mario Mario?”; Miyamoto, on the call, said it was simply Mario. Alistair recited heroic titles and placed the disappearance in 955 BF.
Mario said Peach was alive at the studio. Miyamoto said, “We kept her safe. No assassinations happened here.” Luigi arrived with pizza and joined the effort to send the visitors home.
At the studio, Dr. Takeda announced a dimensional-resonance route home. A portal opened for sixty seconds. Luigi gave the visitors Nintendo charms; Darian recognized his home province. Darian and Alistair passed through. Mario remained in the studio, crying.
The man learns his supposed history from my own article. The paper reports photographs; it does not put a developed photograph in my hands. Do not confuse either with corroboration. — W.
Archive excerpt, deliberately abridged. Original publication details, witness identities, imperial date and the portal's destination remain unverified.

prop_promo_mario_full_account.title: Full Account — Promo Mario (Recovered)
prop_promo_mario_full_account.subtitle: Recovered telling · the rest of the story the clipping cut
prop_promo_mario_full_account.note: The full account reached the archive the same evening as the clipping. It begins where the review ended — and shows the review's ending never happened. Single-source: no publisher, byline, original film or independent witness.
prop_promo_mario_full_account.body:
THE FULL ACCOUNT
Lord Darian Marsh, as told after the fact · archive transcription
Reader: the newspaper printed a farewell. The machine printed PORTAL FAILED. Both statements cannot be filed. I am filing the machine.
I. The portal never opened. Darian and Alistair stepped into warm light, blinked, and were still inside the studio. The machine ran red; Dr. Takeda said the dimensional resonance had been unstable. Nintendo’s plan became recalibration over “a few days.”
II. A tape labeled only 955 BF played a black-and-white funeral: Peach’s casket in purple and gold, a shadowed figure in a black cape at the edge of frame, a glint of metal. Then every monitor showed Luigi drowning, then a black question mark inside a circle, then the tape ejected itself.
III. Luigi was gone when the lights returned. No note, no struggle, no usable footage. Mario ran for the exit with a flashlight and did not come back before the worst of it.
IV. The Wario Show hijacked the studio. Wario came through a television, sang his way through the corridors, dropped the guests into a game-show set, detached his own head, and was finally dispersed by a second press of the Wario Inc. tablet — which is only a flashlight. He last sang about a rotten day.
V. A version of Mario walked out of the television armed with a grudge against a father the studio Mario has never had. It challenged the host to a fight and called the place “MY World.” Darian and Alistair left them fighting.
VI. In the break room, Camera Three showed a figure in green and blue hiding behind crates: wrong hat, wrong height, flickering edges, hollow black eyes. Alistair’s instruction was exact. Don’t go there.
I have filed the clipping as evidence and this as its correction. One source, twice cut. The question-mark signature worries me more than the singing head does. — W.
Transcription, deliberately full where the clipping was abridged. No original page, film, photograph, publisher or independent witness has been authenticated.

prop_wario_inc_tablet.title: Wario Inc. Tablet — The Slate That Read My Own Article
prop_wario_inc_tablet.subtitle: Device record · black glass, purple mark; screen contents transcribed from the full account
prop_wario_inc_tablet.note: A black glass slate marked Wario Inc. in purple. It displayed Waluigi's own biography of the missing hero to the man who may be wearing it. It also carries one unmarked button, which turned out to be a flashlight.
prop_wario_inc_tablet.body:
WARIO INC. TABLET
DEVICE RECORD · SCREEN CONTENTS FROM THE FULL ACCOUNT
MarkingWario Inc., lit across the top in purpleDisplayWaluipedia entry — Mario — Alternate VersionsOnly button on the deviceFlashlight. Pressed twice during the Apparition.
"There might have been a Mario in our world. In our stories." — Lord Darian Marsh, presenting the slate
I. The slate's screen shows the article as the archive filed it: the most famous hero in the Mushroom Kingdom; the man who saved Peach so many times that his name became a verb; the disappearance after eighty-five years of silence; Luigi finding him at the Star Fountain; the flight on wing caps; nothing can hurt us as long as we're together; then gone again, with Luigi at Raventree Manor.
II. Searched later, amid cameras and cold coffee: Mario — Alternate Versions. Multiple timelines load. Some where he disappeared permanently; some where he stayed the hero. At the bottom, a section titled Fallen Maris with one entry: 955 BF — The Disappeared Hero.
"This record begins with the tragedy of 955 BF—not when Peach died, but when Mario vanished without explanation. No body found. No note left. Just... gone. Luigi never recovered after this day."
III. Then the screen glitched and added a line nobody had searched for: WARNING — INCONSISTENT REALITY DETECTED. The studio lights flickered overhead.
IV. The single unmarked button was pressed during the game show. It produced a blinding white flash and a sound like a corrupted file; the Apparition recoiled, and the head came apart pixel by pixel. Pressed a third time, it produced an ordinary flashlight beam.
The most expensive artifact in that world — purchased over my objection, feature list longer than a castle's tax roll — defeated an interdimensional game-show apparition by being a torch. The tablet did nothing. The flashlight won. I am still not over it. — W.
Device not recovered. Screen contents recorded from the full account only; the tablet itself remains in the Hollywood studio per that account, and the account is single-source.

prop_tape_955_bf.title: Tape — One Date: 955 BF
prop_tape_955_bf.subtitle: Media record · found under the studio monitors; contents transcribed from the full account
prop_tape_955_bf.note: A single tape with no title and one date on the label: 955 BF. It played a funeral, then a drowning, then a symbol no one searched for. When it ejected itself, the label was blank.
prop_tape_955_bf.body:
TAPE · NO TITLE
ONE DATE ON THE LABEL: 955 BF
FoundOn a shelf under the studio monitorsLabel before play955 BF — nothing elseLabel after playBlank. Just plastic.
"That's... weird. This must be from Nintendo Mania's fictional timeline." — Mario, before it played
I. The screen flickered and the studio's cheery set vanished behind black-and-white footage: a grainy castle hallway, then a funeral procession, mourners in a style no one present had ever seen, a casket draped in purple and gold — Peach's colors.
II. At the edge of the frame, for one second: a shadowy figure in a black cape, half the face lost in darkness, a glint of metal in hand.
III. Every monitor beeped once, together, and switched to a new picture: Luigi struggling in dark water, bubbles rising, his green cap floating away. Then, across every screen at once, a single symbol — a black question mark inside a circle.
IV. The tape shot out of the player by itself, clattered to the floor, and kept playing on the tiles. Dr. Takeda turned it over. "This... isn't possible." The label was blank now.
The studio's own people said the date did not exist in their timeline. The tape says the assassination and the disappearance were the same year. I let the same number pass me twice. — W.
Tape not recovered; the account places it in the hands of Dr. Takeda's team. Contents recorded from the full account only, and the account is single-source.

prop_studio_security_footage.title: Studio Security Footage — Camera Three
prop_studio_security_footage.subtitle: Feed record · the missing minutes, and the figure behind the crates; transcribed from the full account
prop_studio_security_footage.note: The studio's security feed. During Luigi's disappearance it showed nothing at all, and Dr. Takeda shouted about missing footage. Later, in the break room, Camera Three showed a figure in green and blue that was not Luigi.
prop_studio_security_footage.body:
STUDIO SECURITY FEED
CAMERA THREE · BREAK-ROOM MONITORS
When Luigi vanishedThe feed showed nothing. No struggle, no sound.Next known stateDr. Takeda shouting about energy readings and missing footageWhere the feed was watchedEmployee break room — four monitors, one couch, one cold coffee machine
I. One monitor showed the battle — the version of Mario from the television pinning the studio host to the floor, purple energy crackling around his fists.
II. Camera Three, near the prop room: a figure in green and blue hiding behind crates. Green cap. Blue overalls. Terrified but unharmed.
III. It was not Luigi. The hat was the wrong shade. Too tall. Too still. Its edges flickered once, like a screen losing signal. When the figure turned its head, where Luigi's face should have been were two hollow black eyes.
IV. Neither witness was in the same room as that camera. The one in the room reached through the monitor and waited. The other three monitors went to static, and all four showed the black question mark inside the circle — together, in sequence. Then the coffee machine went cold.
Alistair's instruction was exact: don't go there. An impostor stood exactly where a missing man would be looked for. That is placement, not noise. — W.
Footage not recovered; no frame, no tape, no server record has been authenticated. Contents transcribed from the full account only, and the account is single-source.

prop_belly_torch_test.title: The Torch Test — Two Accounts of One Torch
prop_belly_torch_test.subtitle: Sounding of the pit beneath the jaws · filed from both sides of the trunk
prop_belly_torch_test.note: The party dropped a torch into a hole to learn its depth. The hole complained. Only one person heard the complaint, and she was on the wrong side of the wood.
prop_belly_torch_test.body:
SOUNDING RECORD
One torch · the pit beneath the Scorncrow's jaws · 30 Harvestide, 1040 BF
Outside — as observed. Markop pried the jaws and saw darkness, then a giant pit. He asked whether anyone had a rope. Dan answered that he did not think soooo. A torch was thrown in as a test of depth. The torch came back out of the trunk. No sound, no bottom, no reading.
Inside — as heard by Remi Akamatsu. Voices, in the dark, in a hurry:
there's a fire · someone is causing a fire · they're going to burn us all down
What the two accounts prove together. The party read the returned torch as an unhelpful pit. It was not a pit refusing to be measured. It was an interior that received a fire, understood it as a fire, discussed it in the plural, and sent it back.
Speakers unidentified. Number unknown. Whether they are the wrapped forms hanging from the boughs of the inner tree is not established by this record and should not be assumed by anyone citing it.
Somebody in there said us. Waluigi has read this line eleven times and it has not improved once. — W.

prop_scorncrow_unmasking_note.title: Field Examination — What Was Under the Scorncrow's Face
prop_scorncrow_unmasking_note.subtitle: Point-blank musket discharge by Remi Akamatsu, from beneath the subject · 30 Harvestide, 1040 BF
prop_scorncrow_unmasking_note.note: Three filings called it a monster on its own denial. One shot at zero inches tested the denial. The archive lost that argument and is filing the loss.
prop_scorncrow_unmasking_note.body:
WALUIPEDIA · FIELD EXAMINATION
Subject: the Scorncrow · examination unplanned, conditions adverse, examiner pinned
RangePoint blank — the subject was lying on the examinerInstrumentMusket, one dischargeExaminerRemi Akamatsu, age 14Stated reasoning"Wait a minute. I am at point-blank range."
I. Finding. The discharge removed the face. Beneath it: blood. Human blood.
II. Prior record. The subject has stated I am not a monster on three separate filed occasions. The archive recorded each as taunt and proceeded to describe it as a monster in the same paragraph.
III. Readings available, none preferred. (a) Something human is inside the scarecrow, wearing it, by choice or otherwise. (b) Something human was made into the scarecrow, and the sentence is a complaint. (c) The blood is a further costume, laid over a monster that has learned what this party finds convincing.
IV. Disposition. Subject withdrew into the mouth of its own tree while the examination was still open. No sample retained. No face recovered.
Two of the three readings make that sentence a complaint nobody answered, in a grove where the boughs are hung with wrapped people. Waluigi has stopped using the word monster in this file. — W.
Examination conducted under fire by a combatant, not a physician. Single observer. No custody chain exists for anything described above.

THE MAGES' GUILD — Hall of Audience

prop_cape_note_still_unread.title: The Courier's Note (Unfiled)
prop_cape_note_still_unread.subtitle: One folded leaf · smoke-darkened · contents unknown — the sole reader is missing
prop_cape_note_still_unread.note: Seen in the courier's hand and in the true Luigi's; recovered by nobody. This exhibit records the object, not the text — the text was read exactly once, by a man who is missing.
prop_cape_note_still_unread.body:
EVIDENCE TAG — UNRECOVERED DOCUMENT
Auditor's Office · filed in absence · the file waits
OBJECT: one (1) folded note, folded once, edges smoke-darkened, bearing a leaf-shaped oil stain where the Tanuki Leaf rode against it in the courier's palm.
ATTESTED: delivered to the bridge by the yellow-caped courier at approximately 23:00; pressed into the true Luigi's hand with the words below; read once, in silence, by Luigi alone; carried by him through the lava moat, the leaf-flight, and the vanishing. Never seen again.
“Luigi... read it. Read the note. This changes everything.” — the courier's whole speech, per the auditor's own ears, at a distance of six feet.
I have filed ten thousand papers and this is the only one I ever filed WITHOUT READING, and I think about it every day. Somewhere there is a fold of paper that turned a pursuing brother around mid-stride and sent him flying into the dark past screaming, past rescue, past US — and the only hands that ever held it open are missing. If you find it: do not read it in the field. Bring it to me. Bring it to ME. — W.
Contents unfiled. The sole reader is missing. Any future recovery supersedes this tag.

Unrecovered original · recalled by Luigi after rescue · 18 Harvestide 1035

prop_accords_900_20_containment.title: Autumnwood Accords § 900.20 — Reporting and Remediation Protocols for Unplanned Arcane Interference
prop_accords_900_20_containment.subtitle: The Mages' Guild · handed to a dwarf in a besieged corridor and required to be read on the spot
prop_accords_900_20_containment.note: Six pages. Three thousand seven hundred and twenty-six words. Read to a man with a warhammer in his hand while trees ate the floor below him. None of it was about him.
prop_accords_900_20_containment.body:
THE MAGES' GUILD · AUTUMNWOOD ACCORDS
Part 900 · Unplanned Arcane Interference · § 900.20 Additional Provisions
Extent3,726 words · 6 pagesAuthority§ 900.12, incorporated in fullServed onHjumpik Deldkur, in the fieldServed byColour Division, Iron Legion
(a) Containment and isolation. In the context of unplanned arcane interference, maintaining containment and isolation zones is paramount to ensuring public safety and minimising collateral damage. This section outlines procedures for the ongoing maintenance and monitoring of critical areas established under § 900.20. Proper management ensures that containment measures remain effective over extended periods, reducing the risk of breaches or accidental release of hazardous arcane energies.
(b) Dual focus. Maintenance protocols address structural integrity — the physical state of containment barriers, inspected regularly for deterioration — and environmental stability — monitoring for changes in ambient arcane conditions within and adjacent to isolation zones. Any breach is an immediate threat requiring prompt mitigation under § 1.15.
(c) Instrumentation. Continuous monitoring tools and technologies — arcane sensors, environmental data loggers — shall provide real-time feedback on zone conditions (see § 800.19), permitting early detection of anomalies or shifts in ambient magic levels that could indicate potential breaches.
(d) Personnel. Maintenance personnel designated by the Guild undergo rigorous training. Regular staff rotations and cross-training are mandated under § 1.20 to prevent burnout and skill decay. Containment zone isolation is not a one-time event but an ongoing process requiring periodic re-evaluation (see § 1001.8 for thresholds relating to precious ores).
(e) Emergency protocols. Immediate response plans for breaches or unanticipated surges in arcane energy levels (see § 1.19). Regular drills and simulations are mandated. Any detected anomaly must be reported immediately to the appropriate authorities (see § 800.18), and detailed records of all maintenance activity archived for audit.
Compliance with these procedures not only upholds the integrity of containment zones but also reinforces trust between the Guild and its constituents.
Nothing in this Part shall be construed to limit or impair the full force and effect of any other provision contained herein or in the Autumnwood Accords generally.
Six pages on how to monitor a containment zone, served on a man standing inside one that nobody has declared. He read it. He asked, reasonably, whether they wanted him to monitor this place. They said no — that is what we are tasked to do. Which means the Guild has already classified this manor and did not tell the contractor it left inside it. — W.

prop_aegis_magi_recall_clause.title: Aegis Magi Retrieval Clause — Bound Objects, Recall, and Collateral That Can Walk Away
prop_aegis_magi_recall_clause.subtitle: The clause the Colour Division actually came to enforce
prop_aegis_magi_recall_clause.note: The short document. Two paragraphs, read after the six pages, and the only part of the reading that was about Hjumpik.
prop_aegis_magi_recall_clause.body:
THE AEGIS MAGI · OFFICE OF BOUND ASSETS
Retrieval clause · extract served under the Autumnwood Accords
In the event that a bound object flees its designated location, the Aegis Magi may be authorised to track and retrieve it using “Recall” magic, the costs of which shall be borne by the owner.
Transactions involving objects with high levels of agency — such as golems or sentient constructs — must be overseen by a Guild Notary to ensure that the “binding” is sufficient to prevent the asset from abandoning its legal obligations.
Collateral that can walk away requires extraordinary security; failure to provide such security is a violation of the Accord.
Contract termFive nightsElapsedOverdue; contractor reckons three months, then fiveFindingMission over. Failed.Held againstTwo associates, as insurance
Read the three underlined words and then read them again. Collateral that can walk away. They did not send four operatives across a planar boundary for a report. They sent them for an asset with legs. The dwarf is not the Guild's contractor in this document. He is its security. — W.
